'''Donald Frank Holcomb''' (November 8, 1925 – August 9, 2018) was an American physicist.

Born in [[Chesterton, Indiana]], on November 8, 1925, Holcomb was raised in primarily in [[Wood River, Illinois]], and graduated from East Alton-Wood River High School in 1943. His university studies were interrupted by military service in the United States Navy. After obtaining a bachelor's degree from [[DePauw University]] in 1949, Holcomb pursued graduate study at [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]], completing a Ph.D. in 1954. He began teaching at [[Cornell University]] that same year. In 1964, Holcomb became the third director of the Laboratory of Atomic and Solid State Physics.<ref>{{Cite report|last=Trustees|first=Cornell University Board of|date=1965|title=Proceedings of the Board of Trustees of Cornell University, 1964/1965|url=https://ecommons.cornell.edu/handle/1813/52064|language=en-US|pages=4934}}</ref> In his career, Holcomb spent some time abroad. He received a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] from 1955 to 1957, was named a NATO senior visiting fellow at the [[University of Oslo]] in 1962, a [[Guggenheim fellow]] in 1968 while at the [[University of Kent]], and a [[Science Research Council]] visiting fellow at [[University of St. Andrews]] in 1978. He was granted fellowship into the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref name="cornellchron"/> In 1987 Holcomb became the president of the [[American Association of Physics Teachers]], which also awarded Holcomb its [[Oersted Medal]] in 1996,<ref>{{cite journal |last=Cotts |first=Robert M. |title=Meet Your New AAPT President |journal=The Physics Teacher |volume=25 |issue=2 |pages=74–75 |date=February 1987 |url=https://doi.org/10.1119/1.2342162}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Holcomb |first1=Donald F. |title=''Beyond F=ma,'' Donald F. Holcomb's acceptance speech for the 1996 Oersted Medal presented by the American Association of Physics Teachers, 16 January 1996 |journal=American Journal of Physics |volume=64 |issue=6 |pages=690–693 |doi=10.1119/1.18233|bibcode=1996AmJPh..64..690H |year=1996 }}</ref> a year after his retirement from Cornell.<ref name="cornellchron">{{cite news |last1=Fleischman |first1=Tom |title=Donald Holcomb, emeritus physics professor, dies at 92 |url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2018/08/donald-holcomb-emeritus-physics-professor-dies-92 |access-date=August 26, 2018 |work=Cornell Chronicle |date=August 16, 2018}}</ref> He died at home in [[Ithaca, New York]], on August 9, 2018, aged 92.<ref name="cornellchron"/>
